questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the catalyst used to transform carbon monoxide from water gas into carbon dioxide
questions.solution:
The reaction of carbon monoxide of water gas (syngas) with steam to form carbon dioxide and dihydrogen is called the water-gas shift reaction.

$\text{CO(g)} + \text{H}_2\text{O(g)} \xrightarrow{\text{Iron chromate, } 673\text{ K}} \text{CO}_2\text{(g)} + \text{H}_2\text{(g)}$

The catalyst used in this process is iron chromate.

Answer: Iron chromate

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following oxides is amphoteric in nature?
questions.solution:
$\text{BaO}$ is an oxide of an alkaline earth metal and is basic in nature.

$\text{N}_2\text{O}_5$ and $\text{CO}_2$ are oxides of non-metals and are acidic in nature.

$\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ reacts with both acids and bases to form salt and water, exhibiting both acidic and basic properties. Hence, it is an amphoteric oxide.

Reaction with acid: $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3 + 6\text{HCl} \rightarrow 2\text{AlCl}_3 + 3\text{H}_2\text{O}$

Reaction with base: $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3 + 2\text{NaOH} + 3\text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow 2\text{Na}[\text{Al}(\text{OH})_4]$

Answer: $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the formula of Tin (IV) oxide?
questions.solution:
The oxidation state of Tin (Sn) in Tin (IV) oxide is $+4$.

The oxidation state of Oxygen (O) in an oxide ion is $-2$.

To form a neutral compound, the total positive charge must balance the total negative charge. Two oxide ions are required to balance one Tin (IV) ion.

Using the criss-cross method, the formula is initially $\text{Sn}_2\text{O}_4$, which simplifies to the empirical formula $\text{SnO}_2$.

Answer: $\text{SnO}_2$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from the following is NOT polymorphic form of silica ?
questions.solution:
Silica (SiO_2$) exists in various polymorphic forms such as quartz (\alpha$-quartz and $\beta$-quartz), cristobalite, and tridymite.

Aragonite is a naturally occurring crystalline form of calcium carbonate (CaCO_3$), not silica.

Therefore, Aragonite is not a polymorphic form of silica.

Answer: Aragonite$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the nature of $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$?
questions.solution:
Aluminium oxide ($\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$) is an amphoteric oxide because it reacts with both acids and bases to form salt and water.

Reaction with acid:
$\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3 + 6\text{HCl} \rightarrow 2\text{AlCl}_3 + 3\text{H}_2\text{O}$

Reaction with base:
$\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3 + 2\text{NaOH} + 3\text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow 2\text{Na}[\text{Al}(\text{OH})_4]$

Thus, it is amphoteric in nature.

Answer: Amphoteric

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Identify the catalyst used in following reaction at $500^{{}^{\circ}} \mathrm{C}$ ?
$\mathrm{CO}+\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O} \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{CO}_2+\mathrm{H}_2$
questions.solution:
The water-gas shift reaction is $\mathrm{CO}(\mathrm{g}) + \mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}(\mathrm{g}) \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{CO}_2(\mathrm{g}) + \mathrm{H}_2(\mathrm{g})$, used to produce hydrogen gas from carbon monoxide and steam. Catalyst selection depends on operating temperature.

At high temperatures around $500^{}^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$, the catalyst is an iron-chromium oxide mixture, denoted $\mathrm{Fe}-\mathrm{Cr}$. Iron oxide $\mathrm{Fe}_2\mathrm{O}_3$ serves as the primary catalyst, while chromium oxide $\mathrm{Cr}_2\mathrm{O}_3$ acts as a stabilizer to prevent sintering and maintain activity.

Evaluating the options: $\mathrm{Fe}-\mathrm{Cr}$ is correct for this temperature range. Nickel catalysts are used for hydrogenation, cobalt-thorium for Fischer-Tropsch synthesis, and platinized asbestos for oxidation or hydrogenation—none are standard for high-temperature water-gas shift.

The catalyst is therefore $\boxed{\text{A}}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following metal halide is more covalent?
questions.solution:
Key Idea Fajan’s rules help in predicting the covalent character in bond.
$SbC{l}_{5}$ metal halide is more covalent than other given options. It can be explained on the basis of Fajan’s rule. Higher the charge on the cation, greater is its polarising power. In $SbC{l}_{5},$ Antimony (Sb) is in + 5 oxidation state. It has maximum polarising power. Hence, possess higher covalent character.
